knowledge_point.title: Constructing and Solving a Dilution Model

question.:question/problem:
An aquarium initially holds $100L$ of water containing $3kg$ of dissolved minerals.
A solution containing $0.04kg/L$ of dissolved minerals is pumped into the aquarium at a rate of $8L/min$, while the completely mixed water is drained out at a rate of $12L/min$. If the amount of minerals $Q(t)$, in kilograms, in the tank $t$ minutes after pumping begins is given by
$Q(t) = α(1 - \frac{t}{25}) + β(1 - \frac{t}{25})^{3}$
where $α$ and $β$ are constants, what is the value of $α + β$?

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
question.:question/worked-solution: At $t=0,$ the supplied model gives $Q(0)=\alpha(1-0/25)+\beta(1-0/25)^{3}=\alpha+\beta.$ The initial amount is $3\,\text{kg},$ so $\alpha+\beta=3.$

A solution containing $0.06kg/L$ of dissolved minerals is pumped into the aquarium at a rate of $20L/min$, while the completely mixed water is drained out at a rate of $30L/min$. If the amount of minerals $Q(t)$, in kilograms, in the tank $t$ minutes after pumping begins is given by
$Q(t) = α(1 - \frac{t}{90}) + β(1 - \frac{t}{90})^{3}$
where $α$ and $β$ are constants, what is the value of $α + β$?

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
question.:question/worked-solution: At $t=0,$ the supplied model gives $Q(0)=\alpha(1-0/90)+\beta(1-0/90)^{3}=\alpha+\beta.$ The initial amount is $38\,\text{kg},$ so $\alpha+\beta=38.$
